messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — BERYLLIUM VPC: elevated tail latency observed for dedicated pool be-beryllium. 95/99 latency > 2s, error spike on long-context requests. Paging on-call: @Sally. Incident ID INC-20260315-beryllium.

Sally: Acked. Joining bridge now :rotating_light: pinging SREs and CS.

Mike: On it. Looking at node metrics — be-beryllium-0/1/2 showing CPU saturation + KV cache miss rate up 4x. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/be-beryllium/metrics (private).

Raj: Do we have a suspect tenant or recent deploy?

Mike: Early signal points to tenant-beryllium-corp — sustained large streaming sessions, many long-context evals (30k+ tokens) causing KV thrash and CPU contention. No recent routing deploys.

Sally: Can we isolate that tenant quickly? Prefer moving them to an isolated pool and applying throttles.

Mike: Proposed mitigation steps:
1) Move tenant-beryllium-corp to dedicated-iso-2 (isolation pool) with graceful drain.
2) Apply per-tenant request size throttle and fallback to smaller model for >8k tokens.
3) Monitor latency and error rates.

Commands (exec plan):
```
# move tenant to isolation pool (graceful drain)
redwoodctl routes set --tenant tenant-beryllium-corp --pool dedicated-iso-2 --drain 60s
# enforce token cap for that tenant
redwoodctl policy set --tenant tenant-beryllium-corp --max_tokens 8000
```

Dena: CS has a report from the customer saying some sessions saw increased latency and occasional 502s. Account team looped in.

Lina: Drafting external comms now. Key points to include: what we saw, what we did (isolation + throttles), customer impact estimate, timeline, and proposed credit. Early impact estimate: ~3–10% of requests affected over ~45 minutes; small subset saw 5xxs for very long sessions.

Elena: For the RCA we need sample traces and request ids. Mike, can you attach those?

Mike: Collected sample request ids: req_8f3a, req_8f3b, req_8f4c. Logs show repeated streaming sessions >30k tokens each. Uploading artifacts to /artifacts/beryllium-20260315.tar.gz.

Raj: I'll open a routing-rule PR to add per-tenant adaptive batching + quota for long-context jobs to the dedicated routing policies (prevents single tenant from starving pool).

Alex: Sales/Accounts request an exec summary for the Beryllium CTO. Also asking for guidance on credits — they expect something to offer up-front.

Lina: Proposal in draft: technical RCA + timeline + a customer credit of ~12% (we can negotiate from 15% if needed). Will circulate the draft to @Alex and @Elena for approval before sending.

Sally: Mitigation executed at 2026-03-15T14:12Z — tenant moved, throttles applied. Latency trending back to baseline; continuing to monitor for 2 hours. No further pages right now. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INC-20260315-beryllium status -> mitigated. Post-incident review scheduled: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/INC-20260315

Dena: Outreach update: CS emailed primary contact and scheduled a sync; customer has asked for ETA on RCA and confirmation of permanent protections.

Lina: RCA draft targeted EOD tomorrow. Will include root cause (unbounded long-context workloads from tenant causing KV/cache thrash + CPU exhaustion), mitigation timeline, and recommended config changes (per-tenant caps, routing quotas). Also proposing an update to Dedicated plan SLAs to include optional per-tenant throttling addendum. cc @Elena @Raj

Mike: One follow-up action: enable automated noisy-tenant detection alert we discussed in Q4. Marked as a P1 follow-up and filed INF-3245: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-3245.

Raj: Will put together the PR for routing changes and the test plan (canary + canary-monitor).

Sally: Handing off follow-ups: Lina owns customer comms & credit negotiation, Raj owns routing/config changes, Mike owns artifacts & traces for RCA. On-call resumes normal rotation at 15:00Z. Thanks team — will close thread after RCA shared.
